newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan hopes to appoint a deputy by autumn.
newsitem.headline: Annan hopes to appoint a deputy by autumn.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan said Thursday he would like to be able to appoint a deputy secretary-general by the autumn.
"First of all the post has to be established and it has to be funded," he told a news conference, noting that would require action by the 185-nation General Assembly.
"Ideally, I would want to be in a position to fill the post by the autumn of this year," he said.
There have been widespread reports that former Norwegian Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland is a candidate for the post, once it is created.
Asked whether he had offered her the job, Annan said he had met Brundtland "whom I respect very much and is a very able leader, not only at the national level but at the international level."
"I have no deputy post to offer and therefore did not offer her a post," he said.
"I am on record as saying that I support the creation of a deputy secretary-general's post and I would look very seriously at a woman candidate...I have no candidates at this stage," he added.
He said a deputy would have "across the board" duties, with particular emphasis on economic and social issues.
Ranking immediately after the secretary-general at present are a large number of under-secretaries-general, a rank also held by most of the heads of U.N. specialised agencies.
